name: Accessibility Auto Fixer
description: WCAG accessibility scanner with an admin dashboard, client- and server-side scanning, one-click DOM auto-fixes, and Drush/CI commands.
project_description:
Accessibility Auto Fixer scans Drupal pages for WCAG AA accessibility violations, presents them in an interactive admin dashboard, and applies one-click DOM auto-fixes that persist across page reloads.

It ships two complementary scanners implemented from scratch (no external accessibility engine): a client-side JavaScript scanner (js/scanner.js) that inspects the live DOM and computed styles for missing alt text, unlabelled buttons/links/form fields, and colour-contrast failures; and a server-side PHP scanner (A11yScannerService) that fetches a URL over HTTP and parses the returned HTML with DOMDocument to flag the same classes of issue on inline styles and markup. Results are stored in two custom database tables (a11y_results, a11y_fixes) and surfaced through the admin dashboard at /admin/reports/a11y-dashboard, a full scan log, and a per-scan details page with impact/type filters and per-page history.

Each page receives an accessibility score from 0 to 100, computed by deducting points per violation impact (critical -10, serious -5, moderate -2, minor -1). Every node page gains an 'Accessibility Scan' local task tab that runs the client scanner and opens a slide-in panel listing violations with highlight, single-fix, and fix-all actions; applied fixes are recorded so they no longer resurface on later scans. A 'Scan All' action re-scans previously scanned pages or auto-discovers site routes (up to 500, expanding canonical entity paths) and scans them server-side. Drush commands (a11y:scan, a11y:scan-all) scan one URL or a file of URLs with table or JSON output and a non-zero exit code when violations are found, for CI pipelines. A settings form controls enablement, auto-scan, score threshold, excluded roles, enabled node types, per-check toggles, and CI/report options.
